get.description: Retrieves the list of all Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy rules and any exception rules added to the parent rules

post.description: Creates a new Endpoint DLP policy rule. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.

get.description: Retrieves the list of file types that are available in the Endpoint DLP policy rule criteria. You can create Endpoint DLP rules that apply only to content being sent via specific file types.

parameters.name: external
parameters.description: The file types available to select in an Endpoint DLP policy rule vary depending on whether Content Matching is enabled and DLP engines are used. Setting true for this field retrieves the list of file types available when DLP engines are used with Content Matching enabled. Setting false retrieves a different set of file types available when DLP engines are not used.

get.description: This endpoint is deprecated and is no longer supported for usage. It is replaced by the GET /endPointDlpRules/fileTypeCategories endpoint that retrieves the list of file types available in Endpoint DLP policy rule criteria.

post.description: Adds an exception rule to an existing Endpoint DLP rule. Exception rules allow you to exclude specific users or groups in your organization that need to perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate Endpoint rules. To learn more, Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.

get.description:
Retrieves the list of well-known and discovered endpoint applications. Well-known is a dynamic classification of applications that are frequently seen within the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) security cloud. Applications that are discovered on endpoints by the Zscaler service are classified as discovered applications. To learn more, see About DLP and Endpoint Resources and About Endpoint Context.

Note: The /endPointApplications endpoints are exclusive to API operations related to Application File Access and Clipboard channels. For operations related to other channels, use the /dlpEndpointResource endpoints with appropriate resources.

id.description: System-generated unique identifier for the Endpoint DLP rule

state.description: The current operational state of the Endpoint DLP rule. An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.

order.description: The rule's execution order relative to other Endpoint DLP rules

rank.description: Admin rank value from 0–7 (0 is the highest rank) that determines the rule order you can choose. You can select the rank assigned to you or a lower rank. This field is required when admin rank-based access restriction is enabled.

dlpEngines.description: The list of DLP engines (as name-ID pairs) that must be used for content inspection for this rule. Set NULL to include all DLP engines for this rule. Content Matching must be enabled for the rule to use DLP engines.

fileTypes.description: The file type categories to which the rule applies. The list of available file types changes based on whether you're using DLP engines for content inspection. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all file types. The list of available file types changes based on whether you're using DLP engines for content inspection.

dataTransferMethod.description: The data transfer method or channel targeted by this rule

minSize.description: The minimum file size (in KB) required for rule evaluation. Setting 0 KB removes the minimum data size requirement.

users.description: Name-ID pairs of users to whom the rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all users.

groups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups to which the rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all groups.

departments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments to which the rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all departments.

devices.description: Name-ID pairs of devices to which the rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all devices.

deviceGroups.description: Name-ID pairs of device groups to which the rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all device groups.

deviceTrustLevels.description: The list of device trust levels to which the rule applies. High, Medium, and Low trust level evaluations are applicable only to Zscaler Client Connector traffic, whereas Unknown applies to all traffic. The trust levels are assigned to the devices based on your posture configurations in Zscaler Client Connector. If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation.

timeWindows.description: Name-ID pairs of time windows during which the rule is applied

action.description: The action to perform when the rule triggers

labels.description: Name-ID pairs of labels associated with the rule

externalAuditorEmail.description: The email address of the external auditor to whom Endpoint DLP email alerts are sent

notificationTemplate.description: Notification template used for DLP email alerts sent to the external auditor. This field is required when the auditor information (from a hosted database or external) is provided.

auditor.description: Auditor information from the hosted database specified in name-ID pairs. You can retrieve auditor details from a hosted database using the GET /users/auditors request.

lastModifiedBy.description: Login ID of the user who last modified this rule. This is a read-only field returned only in GET requests.

lastModifiedTime.description: Timestamp of when the rule was last modified. This is a read-only field.

parentRule.description: Parent rule ID applicable when configuring exception rules

endPointApplications.description: The list of endpoint applications to which the rule applies. This field is configurable only for the Application File Access channel.

endPointApplicationGroups.description: The list of endpoint application tags to which the rule applies. This field is configurable only for the Application File Access channel.

resources.description: The list of DLP resources, such as printers, removable storage devices, network shares, and personal clouds to which the rule applies. This field is configurable for Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share, and Personal Cloud Storage channels. The DLP resources are specified in name-ID pairs.

resourceGroups.description: The list of DLP resource tags (as name-ID pairs) to which the rule applies. This field is configurable for Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share, and Personal Cloud Storage channels.

severity.description: The severity of rule violation selected from predefined values. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.

userRiskScoreLevels.description: The user risk score levels to which the rule applies. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.

receiver.description: DLP Incident Receiver details to forward information about content that triggers the policy rule via secure Internet Content Adaptation Protocol (ICAP)

eunEnabled.description: A Boolean value indicating whether end user notifications (EUNs) are enabled for this rule or not

eunTemplateId.description: Unique identifier of the EUN associated with the rule

ucTemplateId.description: Unique identifier of the user confirmation template associated with the rule. This field is configurable only when the Confirm action is selected.

networkType.description: Indicates the network type used by the endpoints based on which the rule applies. This field is configurable only for Network Share and Printing channels.

withoutContentInspection.description: A true value indicates that Content Matching is not enabled, whereas false indicates that it is enabled.

EndpointDlpRule.description: Endpoint DLP policy rule configuring details. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.

parent.description: Parent category of the file type

id.description: System-generated unique identifier for the exception rule

name.description: The rule name is inherited from the parent rule and cannot be modified

state.description: The current operational state of the exception rule. An enabled rule is actively enforced. A disabled rule is not actively enforced but does not lose its place in the rule order. The service skips it and moves to the next rule.

order.description: All parent rules are evaluated. If multiple rules match, the rule with the most restrictive action and highest rule order is applied. Exception rule evaluation stops at the first match, and an exception replaces a parent rule upon match.

rank.description: Admin rank value from 0–7 (0 is the highest rank) that determines the rule order you can choose. You can select the rank assigned to you or a lower rank. This field is required when admin rank-based access restriction is enabled.

dlpEngines.description: The list of DLP engines (as name-ID pairs) that must be used for content inspection for this exception rule. Set NULL to include all DLP engines for this rule. Content Matching must be enabled for the rule to use DLP engines.

fileTypes.description: The file type categories to which the rule applies. The list of available file types changes based on whether you're using DLP engines for content inspection. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all file types. The list of available file types changes based on whether you're using DLP engines for content inspection.

dataTransferMethod.description: This field is inherited from the parent rule and cannot be changed

description.description: Additional information about the exception rule

minSize.description: The minimum size requirement that data must meet before the exception rule applies. Setting 0 KB removes the minimum data size requirement.

users.description: Name-ID pairs of users to whom the exception rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all users.

groups.description: Name-ID pairs of user groups to which the exception rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all groups.

departments.description: Name-ID pairs of departments to which the exception rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all departments.

devices.description: Name-ID pairs of devices to which the exception rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all devices.

deviceGroups.description: Name-ID pairs of device groups to which the exception rule applies. If no specific value is set, the rule applies to all device groups.

deviceTrustLevels.description: The list of device trust levels to which the exception rule applies. High, Medium, and Low trust level evaluations are applicable only to Zscaler Client Connector traffic, whereas Unknown applies to all traffic. The trust levels are assigned to the devices based on your posture configurations in Zscaler Client Connector. If no value is set, this field is ignored during the policy evaluation.

timeWindows.description: Name-ID pairs of time windows during which the exception rule is applied

action.description: The action to perform when the exception rule triggers

labels.description: Name-ID pairs of labels associated with the exception rule

externalAuditorEmail.description: The email address of the external auditor to whom alerts are sent when the exception rule is triggered

notificationTemplate.description: Notification template used for the email alert sent to the external auditor. This field is required when the auditor information (from a hosted database or external) is provided.

auditor.description: Auditor information from the hosted database specified in name-ID pairs. You can retrieve auditor details from a hosted database using the GET /users/auditors request.

lastModifiedBy.description: Login ID of the user who last modified this exception rule. This is a read-only field returned only in GET requests.

lastModifiedTime.description: Timestamp of when the exception rule was last modified. This is a read-only field.

parentRule.description: Parent rule ID for the exception rule. This field is required when configuring an exception rule.

endPointApplications.description: The list of endpoint applications to which the exception rule applies. This field is configurable only for the Application File Access channel.

endPointApplicationGroups.description: The list of endpoint application tags to which the exception rule applies. This field is configurable only for the Application File Access channel.

resources.description: The list of DLP resources, such as printers, removable storage devices, network shares, and personal clouds to which the exception rule applies. This field is configurable for Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share, and Personal Cloud Storage channels. The DLP resources are specified in name-ID pairs.

resourceGroups.description: The list of DLP resource tags (as name-ID pairs) to which the rule applies. This field is configurable for Printing, Removable Storage, Network Share, and Personal Cloud Storage channels.

severity.description: The severity of rule violation selected from predefined values. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.

userRiskScoreLevels.description: The user risk score levels to which the exception rule applies. Selecting no value ignores this criterion in the policy evaluation.

receiver.description: DLP Incident Receiver details to forward information about content that triggers the exception rule via secure Internet Content Adaptation Protocol (ICAP)

eunEnabled.description: A Boolean value indicating whether end user notifications (EUNs) are enabled for this exception rule or not

eunTemplateId.description: Unique identifier of the EUN associated with the exception rule

ucTemplateId.description: Unique identifier of the user confirmation template associated with the rule. This field is configurable only when the Confirm action is selected.

networkType.description: Indicates the network type used by the endpoints based on which the exception rule applies. This field is configurable only for Network Share and Printing channels.

withoutContentInspection.description: A true value indicates that Content Matching is not enabled, whereas false indicates that it is enabled.

EndpointDlpSubRule.description: Exception rule configuration details. Exception rules automatically inherit the channel and rule structure of the parent rule. You cannot assign a different channel to the exception rule, but you can customize most other rule settings. To learn more, see Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules.

id.description: System-generated identifier for the endpoint DLP resource (e.g., printers, network shares, and removable storage devices) or endpoint application

name.description: The name of the Endpoint DLP resource

channel.description: The data transfer method or channel associated with the resource, such as Network Shares, Printers, Removable Storage Devices, and Applications.

isPredefined.description: Indicates whether the Endpoint DLP resource is predefined by the system

networkDriveType.description: The name of the server used for a network drive, if applicable. This field is required if networkDrives is not set.

description.description: Additional information about the endpoint DLP resource

serverName.description: Server name used for network drive. This field is only applicable when configuring a network share resource.

printer.description: Contains the printer configuration for the Endpoint DLP resource. This field is only applicable when configuring a printer resource.

networkDrives.description: Details about the removable storage device configured for the Endpoint DLP resource. This field is only applicable when configuring a network share resource.

removableStorage.description: Removable Storage Device resource details for Endpoint DLP. This field is only applicable when configuring a removable storage device resource.

application.description: Details about the application configured as an Endpoint DLP resource. This field is only applicable when configuring an endpoint application resource.

EndpointDlpResource.description: Represents the DLP resource or endpoint application for a specific channel. This model can contain information about a DLP resource (e.g., printer, network share, or removable storage device) or an endpoint application depending on the API endpoints in which they are used.

id.description: A unique identifier for an entity

name.description: The configured name of the entity

externalId.description: An external identifier used for an entity that is managed outside of ZIA. Examples include zpaServerGroup and zpaAppSegments. This field is not applicable to ZIA-managed entities.

EntityReference.description: This is an immutable reference to an entity that mainly consists of id and name

id.description: System-generated identifier for the DLP resource or endpoint application tag group

channel.description: The data transfer channel type of the tag group

description.description: Additional information about the tag group

resources.description: The list of DLP resources (e.g., printers, network drives, and removable storage devices) or endpoint applications associated with this tag

resourceCount.description: The total number of resources associated with this tag

EndpointDlpResourceGroup.description: Represents a tag that groups DLP resources (e.g., printers, network shares, and removable storage devices) or endpoint applications for a specific channel. This model can represent tags grouping DLP resources or endpoint applications depending on the API endpoints in which they are used.

resourcesToBeAdded.description: IDs of DLP resources to be added to the tag group

resourcesToBeDeleted.description: IDs for DLP resources to be deleted from the tag group

EndpointDlpGroupToResourceAssociation.description: DLP resources to be associated or removed from an existing tag group

resourceId.description: System-generated identifier of the DLP resource for an organization. This is a common ID applicable across DLP resources (e.g., printers, network shares, and removable storage devices) and endpoint applications.

osType.description: The operating system for which the endpoint application is configured

applicationName.description: The display name of the application

bundleID.description: The bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application

filename.description: The name of the executable that runs the application

originalFileName.description: The original file name of the executable, applicable for Windows. This name can be located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.

digitallySigned.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider

modUId.description: The user who last modified the application

lastModifiedTime.description: The timestamp of when the application was last modified

applicationType.description: The endpoint application type as determined by the Zscaler service

version.description: The parent (aggregate) version entry representing 'All Versions'. It presents the overall risk level for the application, which is either the maximum risk level across all child versions or a user-overridden value.

versions.description: The list of individual version entries for the application. Each entry represents a specific version with its own risk level, threat type, and signing status.

deleted.description: Indicates whether the application has been soft-deleted

AssociatedRulesDetails.description: Information about policy rules associated with DLP resources

id.description:
An associated identifier.

Note: This identifier is applicable only for specific features. In other API requests (e.g., policy rule association for endpoint applications), this field is not populated and is shown as null.

osType.description: The operating system for which the endpoint application is configured

z_ver_id_md32.description: This attribute is for Zscaler internal use only. It is a version identifier for a specific endpoint application version.

threatLevel.description: The application's threat level as determined by the Zscaler service

bundleID.description: The bundle identifier that uniquely identifies the application

filename.description: The name of the executable that runs the application

originalFileName.description: The original file name of the executable, applicable for Windows. This name can be located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.

digitallySigned.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider

applicationType.description: The endpoint application type as determined by the Zscaler service

deleted.description: Indicates whether the application has been soft-deleted

groupId.description: System-generated identifier for the endpoint application tag group

description.description: Additional information about the endpoint application tag

modUId.description: The user who last modified the endpoint application tag

lastModifiedTime.description: The timestamp of when the endpoint application tag was last modified

endPointApplications.description: The list of endpoint applications that are included in the tag group

version.description: The version string of the application binary. For the parent entry (aggregate across all versions), this is set to a sentinel value representing 'All Versions'.

z_ver_id_md32.description: This attribute is for Zscaler internal use only. It is a version identifier for a specific endpoint application version.

threat_type.description: The threat type classification for this application version as determined by Zscaler

threat_level.description: The risk level for this version as determined by the Zscaler service

bundle_id.description: The bundle identifier associated with this version

code_signing_certificate_status.description: The code signing certificate status for this version, indicating whether the binary is digitally signed and the signature is valid

threatLevelUpdated.description: Indicates whether the risk level for this version is updated by an admin

IncidentReceiver.description: Information about the DLP Incident Receiver

name.description: The configured name of the Incident Receiver

tenant.description: Name-ID pair of the SaaS application tenant, applicable when the Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding type is used.

unc.description: The Universal Naming Convention (UNC) path to the network printer

ipAddress.description: The IP address of the network printer

domain.description: The domain associated with the printer. This field is optional.

DlpPrinter.description: Represents a printer resource used in Endpoint DLP policy rules

networkPath.description: The full path of the network drive

DlpNetworkDrive.description: Represents a network drive resource used in Endpoint DLP policy rules

vendorId.description: The vendor ID that identifies the manufacturer of the removable storage device

productId.description: The product ID of the removable storage device

serialNumber.description: The serial number of the removable storage device

DlpRemovableStorage.description: Represents a removable storage resource used in Endpoint DLP policy rules

osType.description: The operating system for which the application is configured

fileName.description: The name of the executable that runs the application

originalFileName.description: The original file name of the executable, applicable for Windows. This name can be located on the Details tab in the Properties for the executable file in Windows.

bundleID.description: The bundle ID for the macOS application. Limited to maximum length of 256 characters.

digitallySigned.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the application file must be digitally signed by a trusted provider

DlpApplication.description: Represents an application configured as an Endpoint DLP resource
